extracted.intended_audience: beneficiaries and communication officers of EU-funded Civil Protection actions (project managers, PR/communications staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Visibility and communication rules for press releases and other media outputs produced for EU-funded Civil Protection actions; the manual defines required wording, emblem use, minimum and additional requirements, and related procedures (media clearance, IP, non-compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. INTRODUCTION
rubrics_metrics.description: Introductory section of the Communication and Visibility Manual for Civil Protection Actions funded by the European Union (sets context and scope for visibility/communication requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. EU VISIBILITY
rubrics_metrics.description: Main section covering EU visibility requirements for funded actions (overall rules and principles governing display of EU identity, logos, funding acknowledgement, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.1.1 Derogations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection on derogations — circumstances and rules where standard visibility obligations may be modified or exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.2 Funding statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section dedicated to the required funding statement(s) to appear on communication materials (exact wording prescribed in the manual).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4 Examples of EU emblem and funding statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides concrete examples of how the EU emblem and the funding statement should appear together on materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4.1 Display panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance/examples for applying the EU emblem and funding statement to display panels used in projects (size, placement, layout examples referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4.2 Vehicles, clothing, and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance/examples for marking vehicles, clothing and equipment with the EU emblem and funding statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4.3 Banners
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance/examples for banners (layout, emblem placement and funding acknowledgement examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4.4 Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and examples for including the EU emblem and funding statement in printed publications (reports, brochures, leaflets).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4.5 Digital assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance/examples for digital assets (web banners, PDFs, social graphics) showing emblem and funding statement use online.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.4.6 Stationery, business cards, letterheads, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance/examples for stationery items (business cards, letterheads) regarding emblem and funding statement usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. COMMUNICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Main communication section outlining channels, formats and rules for communicating about funded actions (press/media, digital, visual content).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.1 Press and media engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section on engagement with press and media, including types of interactions and required visibility practice when engaging journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.1.1. Press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific subsection for press releases — prescribes how press releases should be prepared and what visibility/funding acknowledgements and emblem use they must contain.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.1.2. Press conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on organising press conferences and required visibility elements (backdrops, materials, statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.1.3. Media clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for media clearance (approvals, timing, who authorises communications) before public release of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.1.4. Journalist and digital content multipliers visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and guidance for hosting visits by journalists and digital multipliers (visibility requirements during visits and follow-up materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.2 Digital communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Section covering digital channels and how visibility and funding statements should be implemented online.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.2.1. Web communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for website content related to the action, including placement of funding statements, logos, and required pages or notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.2.2. Social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for social media posts about the action (how to reference EU funding, use of emblem, hashtags or disclaimers where required).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.2.3. Photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and guidance for photographic content (attribution, emblem inclusion, captions indicating EU funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.5.2.4. Videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and guidance for video content (credit lines, opening/closing frames with emblem/funding statement, rights clearance).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.6.1 Minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the minimum mandatory visibility elements that must appear on communications (likely including emblem, funding statement and other baseline elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.6.2 Additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists any additional (recommended or conditional) visibility requirements beyond the minimum (branding, co-funding mentions, partner logos).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.7 Non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences and procedures related to failure to comply with the visibility requirements (actions to take, remedial measures, sanctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Section addressing intellectual property issues relevant to communication materials produced for the action (ownership, licences, reuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.2 The EU's right to use communication material
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the EU's rights to reuse or publish communication materials produced under the funded action (licensing/assignment expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3 Moral rights or third-party rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on respecting moral rights and handling third-party rights (permissions, credits, releases).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.5 Templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and use of templates (for press releases, letterheads, banners, etc.) to ensure consistent visibility and correct emblem/funding statement use.

rubrics_metrics.name: code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: References a code of conduct related to communications (ethical and professional standards for engagement and materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.5 Copyright Used in this Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative note about copyright of materials used in the manual (bibliographic/attribution info).
